command: node --import apps/desktop/scripts/test-env.mjs --import apps/desktop/scripts/test-tsx.mjs benchmarks/rust-core/recorders/record-desktop-setting-writes.mjs --tree <git archive of b6f10295a2f698afc85332467192de28500bd146 with node_modules>

entry.notRun: the Electron window (a stand-in answers the zoom calls), config.mjs's own debounce timer and file watch (the forced pass an in-process write starts is run when the call settled), and the notification store
entry.runs: registerWindowSettingsIpc (ipc-window-settings.ts) with the settings store of createDesktopOperations over config.mjs (the local connection), and the operations writeMarkdownDefaultView and updateActivityRailPins of createDesktopOperations

exclusions.activityRailPinsEvent: Node raised 'activity-rail-pins-changed' from its operation; on a core connection the pins reach a client as the config section it reads (`readActivityRailPins`), so the replay compares what the second client reads, not that event
exclusions.bootRewrites: groups odd2, empty, emptyAgent, emptyVolume, emptyRetention, emptyPermissions, emptyPins: their seeds are configs the core's own start-up passes rewrite before any write (the desktop section gets its separation marker, an agent section that is no object is normalised), where Node runs those passes in the app's start-up. The core replay skips them; the Config-level test mixdog-core-config config::service::tests::the_desktops_setting_writes_leave_what_node_left replays every group, these included, from the same recording
exclusions.errorName: a refusal is compared by its message: the window's handler rethrows the error and Electron hands the page the text; Node's class (TypeError, RangeError for the 300-site limit) is not kept across a core connection
exclusions.markdownDefaultViewFile: Node keeps the Markdown default view in <userData>/User/settings.json (a JSONC structural edit); the core keeps it as the config key desktop.editor.markdownDefaultView (editorcfg.rs user scope). For this call the replay compares the answer, the events and what a second client reads, and that the view the core stored is the one Node answered; the config bytes and snapshots are not compared
exclusions.notificationsSubtree: the core keeps Node's notification-preferences.json as the `notifications` subtree of mixdog-config.json; the replay seeds it (last key) and takes it out of the bytes it compares
exclusions.snapshots: the snapshot kinds each call wrote (backups/user-data), as a multiset: the file names carry the time, one process-wide counter and the scope's hash

product.tree: product tree loaded by the recorder
